description: This course aims to introduce the bioinformatics concepts, techniques and tools related to biological databases, sequence analysis, phylogenetic analysis, genomics and protein analysis with a focus on drug discovery application.

syllabus.title: Introduction
syllabus.body: Bioinformatics as an interdisciplinary approach, genome, DNA sequence, central dogma, transcription, translation, DNA structure and modifications.

syllabus.title: Biological Databases
syllabus.body: Types of biological information, biological database search and data retrieval, techniques for extracting DNA sequence, protein sequence and protein structure information, conventions for database indexing and search terms.

syllabus.title: Sequence Alignment
syllabus.body: Pairwise alignment of sequences, scoring matrices, tools for similarity search and sequence alignment, dynamic programming algorithms.

syllabus.title: Phylogenetic Analysis and Genomics
syllabus.body: Introduction to phylogenetics, comparative genomics, orthologs, paralogs, methods of phylogenetic analysis, whole genome analysis, gene prediction, protein structure overview, search and visualization, protein structure and function prediction.

syllabus.title: Drug Discovery
syllabus.body: Technologies and strategies, structural biology and virtual screening for drug discovery, emerging role of biomarkers in drug development, potential drug targets.

outcomes: To search and extract information from different biological databases.
To apply different alignment techniques to biological sequences.
To perform phylogenetic analysis and genome analysis using different tools.
To analyze protein structure and functions.
textbooks: Letovsky, Stanley I., ed. Bioinformatics: databases and systems. Springer Science & Business Media, 2006.
Jones, Neil C., and Pavel A. Pevzner. An introduction to bioinformatics algorithms. MIT press, 2004.
Baxevanis, Andreas D., Gary D. Bader, and David S. Wishart, eds. Bioinformatics. John Wiley & Sons, 2020.
